description: The plot illustrates how classification accuracy (ACC) varies with co-occurrence number for six methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME). The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and uses a logarithmic scale with major ticks shown at approximately 0, 10¹, 10², and 10³, spanning from low single-digit values on the left to several thousand on the right. The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)”, uses a linear scale, and ranges from 60 to 85 with labeled ticks every 5 units (60, 65, 70, 75, 80, 85). The Base series is a black solid line with circular markers, increasing from about 64 at the leftmost point to about 71 at the rightmost point. FT is a blue solid line with downward-triangle markers, rising from about 65.5 to about 73 across the x-range. IKE is a red solid line with upward-triangle markers, increasing from about 67.5 to about 75.2, with intermediate points near 71.8 and 74.3. MEND is a brown solid line with diamond markers, rising from about 70.7 to about 80.1, passing through roughly 75.6 and 78.4. MEMIT is a purple solid line with pentagon markers, increasing from about 69.6 to about 77.6, with intermediate values around 73.8 and 76.9. ROME is a green solid line with square markers, increasing from about 74.4 to about 84.2, with intermediate points near 79.4 and 82.2.
